docs.title: Required claim language
docs.text:
Allowed when exact evidence is green:

  • “matches the pinned Kernel canonical corpus”
  • “recipient-side integrity verification”
  • “issuer authenticity verified against recipient-supplied trusted key” when that exact check succeeds
  • “replay not performed” when execution was not independently replayed
  • “producer-supplied time” when no independent time authority exists

Not allowed from browser parity alone:

  • “same as the Kernel in all semantics”
  • “source is true/authentic”
  • “scanner completed correctly”
  • “decision was authorized”
  • “release/payment is authorized”
  • “trusted timestamp”
  • “independently replayed” when replay was not executed

docs.title: Change control
docs.text:
Any change to paygod-c14n-v1, its canonical source corpus, or decision-critical transport format must:

  1. change through the Kernel first;
  2. create a new reviewed Kernel commit and, where applicable, a new corpus blob identity;
  3. update the website consumer explicitly;
  4. run cross-runtime negative and positive tests;
  5. preserve prior versioned fixtures needed for historical verification;
  6. avoid silently relabeling an older website implementation as compatible.

The corpus Git blob is the strongest identity for exact shared test bytes. Branch names and moving main SHAs are contextual provenance, not substitutes for the frozen blob.

docs.title: Next falsifiable milestone
docs.text:
The next milestone is no longer another local parity vector. It is exact-SHA release correlation:

  1. merge the Kernel-owned corpus and documentation through controlled reviewed PRs;
  2. merge website parity changes in dependency order;
  3. require a push-triggered Website Verifier on the exact merged production-branch SHA;
  4. require Vercel production deployment metadata to point to that exact SHA;
  5. perform live production smoke on the public routes;
  6. record the final merged Kernel and website SHAs in the Observatory evidence record.

Until that release correlation is complete, parity is verified in source/CI but not yet described as deployed exact-SHA production evidence.

docs.title: ADR 0001: Canonical Kernel Records & Schema Validation
Status
docs.text: Accepted

docs.title: Context
docs.text:
Paygod Kernel requires a mechanism to validate data integrity across multiple boundaries (API ingress, internal messaging, ledger storage). The system must guarantee that invalid data is rejected before it can cause side effects or pollute the immutable ledger.

Previously, validation was performed via ad-hoc logic in PowerShell scripts and C# classes. This led to: 1. Inconsistency: Validation rules in the API differed from those in the Ledger. 2. Shadow Validation: Rules existed in code but not in documentation. 3. Maintenance Burden: Every schema change required manual code updates in multiple places.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
We will adopt JSON Schema (Draft 2020-12) as the single source of truth for all data contracts.

The Canonical Record Types defined are: - Observation: Raw input data. - MetricSpec: Definition of how to measure data. - Measurement: The quantified result. - Decision: The final judgment. - Evidence: The bundle of inputs used. - Impact: The consequence/action to take. - LedgerEntry: The sealed record.

Furthermore, we will enforce a Strict Validation Policy: 1. Formats are Assertions: All format keywords (e.g., email, uuid) must be validated strictly. 2. No Unknown Keywords: Schemas must not contain unrecognized keywords (to prevent typos). 3. Unified Engine: A single .NET-based CLI tool (Paygod.SchemaValidator) will be used across all environments (Local, CI, Production) to perform validation.

docs.title: Positive
docs.text:
• Guaranteed Consistency: The same validation logic runs everywhere.
  • Contract-First Development: Developers must define the schema before writing code.
  • Automated Documentation: API documentation can be auto-generated from the schemas.
  • Reduced Liability: Strict format validation prevents common data integrity issues (e.g., invalid emails).

docs.title: Negative
docs.text:
• Initial Friction: Developers must learn JSON Schema syntax.
  • Rigidity: "Quick fixes" to validation logic now require a formal schema update and release.
  • Performance Overhead: Parsing and validating against full schemas is computationally more expensive than simple if checks (though mitigated by Native AOT compilation).

docs.title: Compliance
docs.text: This decision supports Axiom 1: Schema Is Law.

docs.title: References
docs.text:
• SCHEMA_SEMVER_POLICY.md
  • PAYGOD_VALIDATOR_SPEC.md

docs.title: Status
docs.text: Accepted

docs.title: Context
docs.text:
Financial and regulatory systems (like Paygod) operate under strict audit requirements (OSCAL, SOC2). A traditional CRUD (Create, Read, Update, Delete) database model is insufficient because it allows history to be rewritten or deleted, destroying the audit trail.

We need a storage strategy that guarantees: 1. Non-repudiation: Once an action is recorded, it cannot be denied. 2. Traceability: The full history of an entity is preserved. 3. Tamper-Evidence: Any attempt to alter past records is detectable.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text: We will implement an Append-Only Immutable Ledger as the authoritative data store for all decisions and assessments.

docs.title: Key Characteristics:
docs.text:
1. No UPDATE/DELETE: The database user for the application will strictly lack UPDATE and DELETE permissions on ledger tables.
  2. Cryptographic Chaining: Each record will include a hash of the previous record (PrevHash), forming a Merkle-like chain.
  3. Corrections as Append: Modifications are modeled as new "Correction" records that reference the original record ID.

docs.title: Positive
docs.text:
• Audit-Ready: The system is compliant by design. Auditors can verify the integrity of the chain.
  • Debuggability: We can reconstruct the exact state of the system at any point in time.
  • Simpler Concurrency: Append-only writes reduce lock contention compared to complex updates.

docs.title: Negative
docs.text:
• Storage Growth: Database size will grow monotonically. Archival strategies will be needed for very old data.
  • Query Complexity: Fetching the "current state" requires aggregating the history or maintaining a separate "Read Model" (CQRS).
  • GDPR/Privacy: "Right to be Forgotten" is challenging; we must use "Crypto-shredding" (deleting the encryption key) or store PII off-ledger.

docs.title: Compliance
docs.text: This decision supports Axiom 2: Ledger Immutability.

docs.title: References
docs.text: • NIST SP 800-53 (AU-9 Protection of Audit Information)

docs.title: ADR-0003
docs.text: Metric values must reference a MetricSpec.

docs.title: Status
docs.text: Accepted

docs.title: Context
docs.text:
Paygod Kernel requires high performance, strict typing, and enterprise-grade tooling for its core execution engine. However, the DAA (Decision Assessment Assistant) relies on advanced AI/ML capabilities where Python is the dominant ecosystem.

We need to select a technology stack that leverages the strengths of both worlds without introducing excessive complexity.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
We will adopt a Hybrid Polyglot Architecture:

  1. Core Kernel (.NET 8+):
  2. Role: API Gateway, Ledger Management, Validation, Execution.

  3. Why: Strong typing, high performance (JIT/AOT), mature enterprise ecosystem, excellent support for microservices.

  4. DAA Engine (Python 3.11+):

  5. Role: Data Science, LLM Integration, Complex Decision Logic.

  6. Why: Unrivaled library support (Pandas, PyTorch, LangChain), standard for AI workloads.

  7. Communication:

  8. Services communicate via gRPC (internal high-performance) or REST/JSON (external/public).
  9. Strict JSON Schema contracts define the interface between .NET and Python components.

docs.title: Positive
docs.text:
• Best Tool for Job: .NET provides safety and speed for the "plumbing"; Python provides flexibility and power for the "brains".
  • Talent Pool: We can hire specialized .NET engineers for platform work and Data Scientists for decision logic.
  • Scalability: Components can be scaled independently (e.g., scale DAA workers on GPU nodes, Kernel on CPU nodes).

docs.title: Negative
docs.text:
• Operational Complexity: Deployment pipeline must support two different runtimes.
  • Context Switching: Developers working across the full stack must know two languages.
  • Serialization Overhead: Data must be serialized/deserialized when crossing the language boundary.

docs.title: Compliance
docs.text: This decision supports Axiom 3: Zero-Trust Execution (by enforcing strict contracts between components).

docs.title: Status
docs.text: Accepted

docs.title: Context
docs.text: Currently, Paygod Kernel relies on a mix of PowerShell scripts (pwsh/) and Python tools (tools/) for validation, testing, and automation. This fragmentation leads to: 1. Inconsistent Logic: Validation rules might differ slightly between languages. 2. Deployment Friction: Users need multiple runtimes (PowerShell Core, Python 3.x) installed. 3. Performance: Interpreted scripts are slower for high-volume validation in CI pipelines. 4. Developer Experience: Contributors have to learn multiple toolchains.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text: We will consolidate all client-side validation, testing, and interaction logic into a single, unified CLI binary.

docs.title: Technology Choice
docs.text:
• Language: Rust or .NET (AOT compiled).
  • Target: Single static binary (paygod) with no external dependencies.
  • Scope:
  • paygod validate: Schema and policy validation.
  • paygod test: Run pack tests (replacing test_pack.py).
  • paygod build: Package policies into distribution artifacts.

docs.title: Positive
docs.text:
• Zero Dependency: Users just download one binary. No pip install or Install-Module.
  • Speed: Native performance for JSON parsing and policy evaluation.
  • Consistency: One codebase ensures validation logic is identical everywhere.

docs.title: Negative
docs.text:
• Migration Effort: Existing scripts need to be rewritten.
  • Learning Curve: Contributors may need to learn Rust/.NET if they are only familiar with Python/PowerShell.

docs.title: Implementation Plan
docs.text:
1. Define CLI specs in docs/PAYGOD_VALIDATOR_SPEC.md (Done).
  2. Build MVP validator replacing test_pack.py.
  3. Deprecate pwsh/ and tools/ in favor of the new CLI.

docs.title: Status
docs.text: Accepted

docs.title: Context
docs.text: We are adopting an Open Core business model. This requires a technical architecture that allows us to develop a public, open-source "Kernel" while simultaneously building proprietary "Enterprise" extensions. We need a strategy to manage codebases, dependencies, and build pipelines without leaking commercial IP or crippling the open-source project.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text: We will use a Multi-Repository Strategy with strict dependency direction.

docs.title: 1. Repository Structure
docs.text:
• paygod/kernel (Public): The source of truth for the core engine. Contains:
    • Core Logic (.NET/Rust)
    • Public CLI (paygod)
    • Public Schemas & Contracts
    • Community Packs
    • Open Documentation
  • paygod/enterprise (Private): The commercial product. Contains:
    • Management Dashboard (UI/Frontend)
    • SaaS Infrastructure (IaC)
    • Enterprise Connectors (AWS/Azure Integrations)
    • Multi-tenant API Services
    • Proprietary License Manager

docs.title: 2. Dependency Flow
docs.text:
Direction: Enterprise depends on Kernel. NEVER the reverse.

  • The Kernel builds and publishes versioned artifacts (Nuget packages, Rust Crates, Docker Images).
  • The Enterprise repo consumes these artifacts as standard dependencies.
  • Extension Points: The Kernel exposes clean Interfaces/Traits (e.g., ILedgerStore, IPolicySource) that the Enterprise version implements to inject advanced capabilities (e.g., replacing a local file store with a centralized database).

docs.title: 3. Build & Release
docs.text:
• Kernel Release: Triggers a public GitHub Release + Package Registry upload.
  • Enterprise Release: Triggers a private build that pulls the latest stable Kernel package, wraps it with proprietary modules, and deploys to the SaaS environment.

docs.title: Positive
docs.text:
• Security: Impossible to accidentally commit proprietary code to the public repo.
  • Clarity: Clear separation of concerns. Open source contributors are not confused by "stubbed" or "locked" features.
  • Licensing: Clean boundary. Apache 2.0 applies to everything in kernel. Commercial license applies to everything in enterprise.

docs.title: Negative
docs.text:
• Complexity: Requires managing two CI/CD pipelines and synchronizing versions.
  • Refactoring Friction: Changing a core interface in kernel requires a coordinated update in enterprise.

docs.title: Compliance
docs.text: To ensure this strategy works: 1. No "If Enterprise" flags in Kernel: The Kernel code must not contain logic like if (isEnterprise). Instead, it should use dependency injection or plugin interfaces. 2. Public API First: Any feature needed by Enterprise must be exposed via a public API/Interface in the Kernel.

docs.title: 1. Overview
docs.text: Paygod.SchemaValidator is a standalone .NET 8 CLI tool (and library) designed to serve as the Unified Validation Engine for the Paygod ecosystem. It enforces "Schema is Law" by strictly validating JSON data against JSON Schemas with strict format assertions.

docs.title: 2. Core Objectives
docs.text:
• Strictness: Enforce format keywords as assertions (e.g., email, date-time, uuid).
  • Performance: Native AOT compilation for sub-second startup and execution.
  • Portability: Single-file binary distribution for Linux (CI/Container) and Windows (Dev).
  • Integration: Designed to be called by PowerShell scripts, GitHub Actions, and Docker containers.

docs.title: 3.1 Technology Stack
docs.text:
• Language: C# (.NET 8.0)
  • Core Library: JsonSchema.Net (by Greg Dennis) - chosen for compliance with Draft 2020-12.
  • CLI Framework: System.CommandLine or simple args parsing.

docs.title: 3.2 CLI Interface
docs.text: paygod-validator validate --schema <path_to_schema> --instance <path_to_data> [--output-format <text|json>]

docs.title: Arguments:
docs.text:
• --schema, -s: Path to the JSON Schema file (required).
  • --instance, -i: Path to the JSON data file to validate (required).
  • --output-format, -o: Output format. Defaults to text (human readable), json for machine parsing.

docs.title: Exit Codes:
docs.text:
• 0: Validation Passed.
  • 1: Validation Failed (Schema violations found).
  • 2: Application Error (File not found, Invalid JSON syntax, etc.).

docs.title: 4.1 Strict Format Validation
docs.text:
The tool MUST configure the underlying validation engine to treat formats as errors.

// Configuration Concept
var options = new ValidationOptions
{
    OutputFormat = OutputFormat.Detailed,
    RequireFormatValidation = true // CRITICAL: This enables strict format checking
};

docs.title: 4.2 Error Reporting
docs.text:
Output must be clear and actionable.

Text Output Example:

[FAIL] Validation failed for 'user_profile.json'
Errors:
  - /contact/email: 'not-an-email' is not a valid email address.
  - /meta/uuid: Value must match format 'uuid'.

JSON Output Example:

{
  "valid": false,
  "errors": [
    {
      "path": "/contact/email",
      "message": "'not-an-email' is not a valid email address",
      "keyword": "format"
    }
  ]
}

docs.title: 5. Implementation Plan
docs.text:
1. Scaffold Project: Create src/Paygod.SchemaValidator console app.
  2. Install Dependencies: Add JsonSchema.Net.
  3. Implement Logic:
  4. Load Schema & Instance from file paths.
  5. Configure ValidationOptions.
  6. Execute schema.Evaluate(instance, options).
  7. Parse results and render output.
  8. Build & Publish: Configure csproj for PublishAot=true.

docs.title: 6. Future Extensions
docs.text:
• Remote Schemas: Support fetching schemas from HTTP/S URLs.
  • Batch Mode: Validate multiple files in one run for performance.
  • Watch Mode: Re-run validation when files change (for dev experience).

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text: This page describes the architecture of the PayGod Kernel.

docs.title: Core Components
docs.text:
The PayGod Kernel is composed of the following core components:

  • Kernel: The core of the system, responsible for managing packs and processing transactions.
  • Packs: Extensible modules that provide specific functionalities, such as payment methods or workflows.
  • Contracts: Data contracts that define the structure of the data exchanged between the kernel and the packs.

docs.title: High-Level Architecture
docs.text:
The following diagram illustrates the high-level architecture of the PayGod Kernel:

graph TD
    A[Client Application] --> B(PayGod Kernel)
    B --> C{Packs}
    C --> D[Payment Gateway]
    C --> E[Ledger]

docs.title: Contracts
docs.text: This page describes the data contracts used in the PayGod Kernel.

docs.title: Introduction
docs.text: Data contracts are used to define the structure of the data exchanged between the kernel and the packs. They are defined using JSON Schema.

docs.title: Core Contracts
docs.text:
The following are the core data contracts used in the PayGod Kernel:

  • Transaction: Represents a payment transaction.
  • Ledger: Represents a ledger of transactions.
  • Pack: Represents a pack that provides a specific functionality.

For more details on the data contracts, please refer to the JSON Schema files in the contracts/ directory of the repository.

docs.title: Evidence Integration Kit (EIK) — developer and coding-agent entry
docs.text:
Status (2026-10-14): documented local entry plus a merged, executable synthetic GitHub Actions reference. PR #112 added a saved synthetic-report reference with canonical CLI and recipient-side CI witnesses; see the dated technical status. The source and outcome are bounded to synthetic fixtures, not an external user acceptance or a live scanner. EIK is not a packaged SDK, live GitHub scanner connector, hosted service, autonomous Pack authoring agent, MCP server, A2A endpoint, certified deployment gate, or public marketplace.

Principle: Build privately. Verify independently. Contribute optionally.

This guide is designed for developers and coding agents who know their own problem better than the PayGod maintainers. You do not need to submit an upstream PR, disclose your Pack, connect a PayGod account or deploy a PayGod service just to test a local Pack.

docs.title: 1. Discover the truthful compatibility surface
docs.text:
• Public implementation and limits
  • Dated claims register
  • Pack definition contract
  • Policy examples and non-claims
  • Canonical recipient verifier
  • Agent contribution instructions
  • Machine-readable discovery snapshot — informational, not a versioned Kernel schema or endorsed agent protocol.

First ask: what does the user's native platform already prove? What does it lack? There is no reason to add PayGod if the native tooling already solves the need with equal assurance and less cost.

docs.title: 2. Choose the right extension surface
docs.text: Need First suitable location Explicit boundary A domain-specific policy Private/local Pack (pack.yaml plus tests/cases.yaml) Kernel still owns the canonical evaluation output Missing, stale, impossible or unsupported observations Pre-Kernel admission, read-only mapping or fixture WITHHELD / NOT RUN external to Kernel; never invent a verdict Source retrieval or provider lifecycle Optional source-specific adapter Do not forge authorization, provenance or receipts Common policy evaluator/receipt semantics actually defective Separate evidence-driven Kernel issue/ADR New semantics require guarded approval and compatibility witnesses Recipient needs stronger source truth / independent time External evidence/authority and a specific verification test The existing integrity verifier alone does not provide these

docs.title: 3. Build your first private Pack
docs.text:
Prerequisites: .NET 8 and Python 3.11+ for the documented tools. Use a disposable working directory or branch; pack init writes into packs/core/ unless a provider is selected.

dotnet run --project src/PayGod.Cli -- pack init --name local-evidence-example
python3 -m pip install -r tools/requirements.txt
python3 tools/pack_validate.py
dotnet run --project src/PayGod.Cli -- test --pack packs/core/local-evidence-example --json

Replace the example rules with rules matching your policy. Design at least these test classes: accepted true/false input, missing required field, wrong type, source error masquerading as a clean report, contradictory source, and tampered evidence. The CLI policy fixture test can compare its declared decisions, but it is not a universal pre-Kernel admission validator.

An optional structural-only preflight is available for Packs that declare an explicit object schema with nonempty required fields. Write a local JSON fixture such as {"input":{"block":false}} for the generated example, then run:

python3 tools/eik_admit.py --pack packs/core/local-evidence-example --input input.json

The tool returns STRUCTURAL_ONLY_PASS for correctly typed declared fields, or WITHHELD_NOT_RUN (exit code 2) for missing/malformed inputs. It never invokes Kernel or asserts scanner success, source truth, temporal validity or external execution authority. A structural pass alone must not trigger production run. Provider-specific source completion, authenticity, provenance and any explicit mandate need separate admission checks.

Critical current limitation: generic run does not automatically enforce every embedded Pack input schema. A Pack schema valid under pack_validate.py is not proof of source truth, runtime mandatory-field completeness, or a safe production decision. Perform admission before invoking run; for missing required evidence the external orchestrator must report WITHHELD / NOT RUN and not call Kernel. See ADR 0003.

Do not treat a generated Pack's illustrative allow result as deployment permission. The external system and its owner retain operational release authority.

docs.title: 4. Optional authorized evidence run and handoff
docs.text:
After independently establishing admission for a complete compatible input, the canonical CLI can be exercised with a deliberately fixed fixture. Example command shape (not a runnable proof without that admitted input and a selected Pack):

dotnet run --project src/PayGod.Cli -- run --pack packs/core/<your-pack> --input <admitted-input.json> --out <evidence-dir>

Use standalone verifier documentation to verify a transferred directory and optionally pin the expected receipt SHA-256 using a separately delivered commitment. Integrity verification does not prove source authenticity, external organizational authorization, independent clock time, replay, or the truth of the represented observation.

docs.title: 5. Optional contribution to the public repository
docs.text:
Contribute only if useful to others, with a small isolated diff under the existing Apache-2.0/DCO process. Include: - Problem, native alternative, and precise scope. - Source type, consent and explicit admission rule; no secrets or private data. - Positive and negative cases including missing/incorrect evidence. - Commands and exact revision to reproduce tests. - If applicable, independent verifier result and explicit non-claims. - No required PayGod account/service, payments, permanent fork, or modification of another team's project.

Read CONTRIBUTING.md before submitting. A merged Pack is not production certification, a commercial listing, financial reward, or proof that the author's domain policy is substantively correct.

docs.title: 6. Synthetic GitHub Actions reference and open external tests
docs.text:
A narrow, runnable synthetic saved-report example is available at examples/eik-github-actions. It calls the actual CLI after two admission checks, then verifies a transferred canonical bundle and adversarial cases. This is not a live scanner integration or proof that an unfamiliar developer/independent external organization completed it.

The real-world E-004 hypothesis remains unproven until a new user/agent and recipient test on permitted, real sources and a counterfactual against GitHub's native controls.

docs.title: 7. Forward-compatible discoveries
docs.text:
The private Observatory tracks EIK as H-007 / E-004 / W-02: compare local user/agent setup and source-admission rejection against native GitHub Actions / direct CLI, then repeat on a second distinct source. Count human interventions, false admission, engineering hours and independent recipient comprehension. Continue source-specific research in parallel; no upstream maintainer is required to install PayGod.

A future published skill, discovery service or MCP tool may consume these public docs and bounded contracts. No chatbot is expected to auto-discover PayGod today merely because this file exists.

• No live GitHub security-scanner API integration or genuine scanner-report source authentication in the reference.
  • No independently recruited developer/AI agent onboarding result or externally consenting recipient test.
  • No measured improvement versus direct CLI and GitHub's native reviews, protection mechanisms and artifact attestations.
  • No autonomous EIK capability planner, SDK, MCP server, A2A endpoint, Pack marketplace or managed deployment gate.
  • No universal pre-Kernel input-schema enforcement at the generic run entrypoint. Issue #111 records potentially unsafe untyped expression comparisons requiring separate, version-aware resolution.
  • No demonstrated bank/payment release, independently trusted clock, source truth, institutional authorization, compliance certification or commercial uptake.

docs.title: Next falsifiable acceptance requests
docs.text:
1. Unknown developer/agent: install nothing beyond documented prerequisites, build a private Pack or replay the synthetic reference without personal PayGod guidance; record time/interventions and where the guide fails.
  2. Authorized genuine source: save an existing scanner report with exit and completion status, document permission and complete semantics; verify missing/failed results remain pre-Kernel WITHHELD/NOT RUN.
  3. Independent recipient: receive only canonical artifacts and a genuinely independently conveyed expected receipt commitment; report which trust dimensions were verified versus unsupported.
  4. Native counterfactual: compare resulting effort and recipient understanding against GitHub-native protections/attestations plus direct CLI; record NO DIFFERENTIAL VALUE if applicable.

Result today: an executable synthetic reference with a bounded CI witness, not a passed independent external E-004 pilot or a production release authorization.

docs.title: Getting Started with PayGod Kernel
docs.text: Authoritative onboarding: START_HERE.md. The commands below are introductory and do not replace the pinned witness and CI test instructions there.

docs.title: Build the canonical CLI
docs.text:
Prerequisite: .NET SDK 8.

git clone https://github.com/hamadalmunyif/paygod-kernel-mvp.git
cd paygod-kernel-mvp
dotnet publish src/PayGod.Cli/PayGod.Cli.csproj -c Release -o out

The canonical CLI can validate, test and run compatible policy packs. See the example commands in START_HERE. Use the versioned paygod-c14n-v1 profile: external fractional measurements cannot be silently passed as JSON decimal values into canonical decision hashes.

docs.title: Independent verification
docs.text:
The standalone Python verifier can verify transferred manifest/receipt/ledger/file integrity without rerunning the originating policy. It supports an optional detached Ed25519 receipt signature under a recipient-owned trust store. See Standalone Verifier.

For real/deidentified sources, apply ADR 0003 before evaluation: unavailable/unrepresentable mandatory evidence produces orchestration NOT RUN, not a forged FALSE.

docs.title: Contributing
docs.text: Read Contributing, Gates and the active Stop-Build. This repository is the canonical public implementation. External research results do not become installed Kernel features by publication alone.

docs.title: Introduction — PayGod Kernel
docs.text:
PayGod Kernel is a deterministic, contracts-first policy/decision core. Its current supported output is schema-governed decision evidence: portable artifacts, manifest and receipt commitments, a hash-linked ledger, and a standalone independent integrity verifier.

The optional Ed25519 receipt signature authenticates the committed receipt under a recipient-supplied key. Neither a matching digest nor a verified signature proves the external source fact, regulator approval, or permission to execute a financial transaction.

The Kernel is not a complete payment processor, bank switch, production custody provider, enterprise SSO service or regulator-approved compliance system.

Start with current implementation and explicit non-claims, quickstart, architecture and research transfer boundaries.

docs.title: PayGod Open Collaboration — Parallel Evidence-Governed Program
docs.text:
Status: ACTIVE as of the accepted 2026-10-14 PR #108; supersedes only the prospective blanket stop-build. The earlier rule and frozen witnesses remain in Git history. Open independently scoped exploration while protecting canonical authority and release gates.

Operating rule: Upstream First · Evidence Native · PayGod Optional.

Build privately · Verify independently · Contribute optionally. Personal/agent-authored Packs can be developed and tested without creating a PayGod PR or account. The EIK entry guide is documentation and a local onboarding path, not a released adapter SDK, hosted assessment, authenticated source, or deploy authorization.

docs.title: Four separate authorities
docs.text:
1. Upstream maintainer accepts/releases their own source; our PR is never automatic adoption.
  2. External runtime/rail owns native execution, identity, and settlement.
  3. Canonical PayGod Kernel alone owns its registered decision and evidence identity.
  4. Independent verifier checks defined recipient-side evidence only, never inventing fact, time, or authorization.

docs.title: Parallel work lanes, with independent GO/HOLD/STOP
docs.text:
Lane Home What can advance now Gate specific to its claims Canonical integrity and defect fixes Kernel repair, reproducibility and bounded security work witness, protected CI, owner review; semantic ADR B2-REAL / gas acceptance gas case register + Observatory solicit and evaluate genuinely eligible cases/recipients frozen B2 qualification; not prerequisite for other lanes External Virtuals X1 Observatory + pinned X1 materials read-only capture, prospective shadow design spend approval before paid job, no Kernel promotion by inference AP2 blind Pass B isolated neutral handoff independent review and falsifiers blinded isolation; preserve Pass A and history OSS native contributions temporary fork/upstream PR reproduce and improve external native bugs upstream maintainer controls merge/release Optional adapters / cross-protocol Observatory fixtures, read-only comparisons, negative tests upstream authority stays external; no forged receipt CEMS/GHG industrial data Observatory read-only/deidentified data and numeric-admission research source quality, permission, domain-specific acceptance Nondeveloper handoff Observatory portable evidence, independent recipient exercises recipient's documented scoped verification result Buyer discovery private research records needs interviews, counterfactuals, pilot design buyer or partner statements, not inferred demand Website/public claims Cloud describe accepted evidence accurately claim register, deployment-specific witness

A HOLD on one lane never blocks another unless a documented dependency is technically necessary. A success in one lane never waives another lane's acceptance or authorization gate.

docs.title: Minimal interaction contract
docs.text:
Upstream event / saved JSON / measurement → preserve raw bytes and source → provenance-labeled optional adapter → pre-Kernel admission (WITHHELD/NOT RUN outside Kernel for missing mandatory facts) → unchanged canonical Kernel when representable → portable evidence → independent scoped verifier → compare against native status.

Adaptation is optional; do not require upstream to install PayGod, change protocol, accept a fork, transfer secrets, or trust a PayGod receipt. Prefer no checkout, narrow reads, and native fixtures when available.

docs.title: Work ownership
docs.text:
• Kernel = sole canonical implemented PayGod decision/receipt/manifest/bundle source.
  • Private Observatory = hypothesis and decision registry, experiments, independent review isolation, and shadow integrations; never public proof by mere existence.
  • Cloud starter = non-authoritative website and presentation. Its default branch is master.
  • Upstream projects = code and release authority for their own projects.

Do not create new repositories solely to reopen a lane. Use disposable branches/forks only for a proved native change.

docs.title: Routing and review
docs.text: Each lane tracks: source URL + SHA/date, objective, falsifier, data permission, authority boundary, acceptance gate, owner, blocked reason if any, direct hours, upstream waiting days, current claim ceiling and next permitted action. Review lanes concurrently. Only semantic Kernel promotion requires a dated ADR and protected checks; defect/security repairs follow the documented protected path.

docs.title: Decision rules
docs.text:
• GO: scoped authorized next experiment or upstream-native bug fix with verifiable outcome.
  • HOLD: missing permission, witness, reviewer independence, or rail-level authorization for that lane only.
  • STOP: unverifiable claims, forged receipts, undisclosed spending, bypass of upstream controls, confidentiality violations or inadequate bounded risk.

Continue independently useful work while a foreign PR is awaiting response. Submitted, reviewed, merged, released, adopted and externally verified are distinct states.

References: Scoped Stop-Build Amendment, Claims, CMP-01, Targets, Registry, Roadmap.

docs.title: CMP-01 — Contribution-to-Merge Protocol
docs.text: Status: PROPOSED. Reusable process, not an upstream rule or an automatic right to merge. Follow each upstream CONTRIBUTING, LICENSE, CODEOWNERS, SECURITY, CLA/DCO, branch protections and release requirements first.

docs.title: Eight verifiable stages
docs.text:
1. DISCOVER — Confirm upstream is active and correct repo/branch. Capture issue URL, current main SHA, license, review convention and native control that may already solve the need. Do not fork based only on an attractive idea.
  2. REPRODUCE — Pin upstream revision, run its own tests, provide minimal positive and negative witness. Report limitations including dependencies, credentials and unavailable network evidence.
  3. BOUNDARIES — Identify who controls user consent, roles, API authorization, wallet/rail, money, data retention, object identity, timestamps and release. Build a concrete affected-surface inventory (code, API, schema, CLI output, docs, on-chain semantics, logs, CI).
  4. DESIGN — Choose upstream-native fix with smallest viable diff. Confirm that requested behavior is not already implemented. Write non-goals. Changes to wire/state/rail/authorization require upstream issue-first consultation.
  5. FORK/BRANCH — Fork only if write permission is absent AND code is needed. Create one short-lived branch from pinned upstream base, and keep the upstream remote. Never merge upstream main into a long-lived incompatible PayGod fork. Use read-only sample/adapters for exploratory projects.
  6. VALIDATE — Native build/typecheck + regression that fails before fix and passes after + adversarial negative tests. Include compatibility and fail-closed behavior. For external service semantics (e.g., PUT update), mark unverified until server/test-double or authorized sandbox validates.
  7. SUBMIT/REVIEW — One problem per PR. Include 'why', issue link, tests and exact reproduction, changed authority boundary, threat model, non-goals, expected API/UX changes, upstream commit reference, and any required changelog entry. Respond to feedback with evidence. Submit only when patch is useful independently of PayGod.
  8. VERIFY OUTCOME — Differentiate SUBMITTED, REVIEWED, APPROVED, MERGED, RELEASED and ADOPTED. Independently check upstream main commit, release tag/package and actual behavior. Closed-unmerged is not rejected on merits unless the maintainer says so.

docs.title: Control matrix by changed surface
docs.text: Surface touched Required negative or compatibility witness CLI flags / headless execution No TTY; missing required flag; machine-readable error; no stale prompts; old interactive mode preserved Update API Unknown ID; whitespace-only fields; omission/false/null tri-state; field preservation in true backend; retries/concurrency Delete API Wrong ID; repeated deletion; missing confirmation; explicit noninteractive consent; permissions; auditability Events / retry Unknown result, duplicate delivery, idempotency key reuse, reordering, partial failure Agent evaluation Provider-controlled prompt/data isolation; evaluator identity; signature does not prove independent judgment Signed transcript Correct DID/key; canonical bytes; venue-time metadata separate from signer time; replay and disputed ordering Settlement Native chain/rail observation; finality/reorg where applicable; reconciliation with claimed protocol status PayGod evidence File/receipt/ledger digest mutation; detached trust-key binding; no local receipt manufacture by adapter

docs.title: Fork policy
docs.text:
• No fork for reading, watching, discussing, writing interoperability documentation, or submitting a non-code issue.
  • Temporary fork for a confirmed upstream bug or accepted narrow improvement requiring code; track upstream base/head and keep history intact.
  • Research sandbox if the question is about cross-protocol behavior rather than changing upstream. Prefer fixture import and read-only observers.
  • Never fork to impose PayGod: upstream gets a self-contained benefit without a PayGod SDK, token, service, branding, account, required API, paid call, or mandatory network permission.
  • Long-lived fork requires separately documented upstream incompatibility, security/maintenance owners and exit strategy. Default is no.

docs.title: Upstream-first review message structure
docs.text:
Title: fix/test/docs(subsystem): observable behavior.

Body: - Problem and user impact (link to independently reported issue). - Reproduction on pinned upstream base; exactly what fails. - One-paragraph smallest patch and non-goals. - Tests: exact commands, exit results, failing-before/green-after evidence. - Authority/compatibility/security impacts: explicit if none. - No mandatory PayGod integration or hidden dependency. - Ask: one specific maintainer judgment. Respect CLA/security reporting instructions.

Feedback never means automatic adoption. One courteous follow-up after a material test improvement or a reasonable review interval; no mass tagging or demand for review.

docs.title: Strict rule for disclosure
docs.text: Do not publish exploitable vulnerabilities or confidential user data into public PRs; follow upstream SECURITY.md and private advisories. Do not upload API keys, wallet keys, nonpublic Observatory data, full customer logs, or personal contacts.

docs.title: CMP-01 application to Virtuals ACP CLI PR #105
docs.text:
Actual external PR: https://github.com/Virtual-Protocol/acp-cli/pull/105 Linked reporter issue: https://github.com/Virtual-Protocol/acp-cli/issues/79 Head SHA reviewed: 5526b606f55739aa675cd7e5a1e62ab4d45c0f59

Confirmed source-level risks to resolve or explicitly bound before asking for merge: - Whitespace-only update name/description may be trim-converted to empty strings. Server rejection/acceptance is unverified. - --resource-id plus --force removes CLI confirmation by design. Identify this authorization/UX change in PR. - Resource update sends a Partial body via HTTP PUT. Backend preservation of omitted fields is NOT proven by TypeScript. - Headless delete WITHOUT --force still attempts readline; fail promptly instead of hanging in no-TTY contexts. - 'No changes made.' in --json mode is plain text, violating machine-readable result expectation.

Tests to add first: no-TTY update success; invalid/missing resource ID; whitespace-only name/description/url; partial field preservation at API boundary; hidden/no-hidden/absent tri-state; no-op with --json; no-TTY delete without force; with force exact-target deletion and double-delete; original interactive behavior. An upstream-native regression or approved authorized mock is required for any claimed server behavior. Avoid patching paygod-kernel-mvp as a substitute.

docs.title: Independence and claims
docs.text: Native platform controls may already solve much of the problem; compare them as a baseline. A shadow PayGod witness is not a native enforcement guarantee. The verifier proves only stated checks. Demonstrated synthetic behavior does not become a production, regulatory or financial claim. See docs/CLAIMS_REGISTER.md.

docs.title: 2026-10-14 — parallel integration rule (proposed)
docs.text:
CMP-01 is an upstream contribution protocol, not a dependency gate on PayGod's observational experiments. Run two independent lanes:

  • Native upstream lane: reproduce an upstream problem, test and propose a minimal dependency-free fix. Only the upstream maintainer may merge and release it. External review waiting time is recorded, never converted into an internal product freeze.
  • Optional local interoperability lane: capture legally accessible original bytes or supplied fixtures; do read-only, provenance-labeled adaptation and independently test a PayGod shadow result. Never rely on unmerged upstream behavior as though available in production.

A cross-lane dependency is recorded only if a concrete interface or permission makes it technically unavoidable. B2, X1, AP2 Pass B and CEMS each have independent claim gates. Exploratory Kernel candidates remain non-canonical until witness → ADR → protected tests → approval.

Every case must record scope, source_ref, falsifier, authority_boundary, permission, next_action, blocking_dependency (if any), engineering_hours, external_wait_days and evidence_ceiling. Do not bypass privacy, secrets, payment authorization or upstream SECURITY instructions.

docs.title: Parallel 90-day roadmap — Evidence-governed, upstream-first
docs.text: Status: proposed 2026-10-14 amendment on PR #108. Each lane advances independently subject to its own authority/evidence gate; this plan neither orders spending nor releases production.

docs.title: Days 0–7: establish the decision boundary and unblock concurrent work
docs.text:
• Review PR #108 as an explicit prospective governance change; confirm frozen evidence files were not changed. Main remains under current rule until approved merge.
  • Preserve Kernel canonical CI and independent-verifier witnesses; triage #107 legal provenance and #103 GHG as distinct draft decisions.
  • Improve external Virtuals ACP CLI #105 with upstream-native red/green regressions: no-TTY, blank fields, omitted field preservation through PUT, JSON no-op, deletion and idempotency. Request maintainers' review only after tests.
  • Start in parallel, without waiting for #105 or B2 quotas: B2 qualified real-case sourcing, nondeveloper verifier handoff, isolated AP2 Pass B, Virtuals X1 read-only acquisition, CEMS measurement source/decimal profile experiment, and one buyer/recipient interview.
  • For each lane record source pin, scope, falsifier, permission, owner, metrics and known blockers. No fabricated outcomes.

docs.title: Days 8–30: test reuse across two independent foreign surfaces
docs.text:
• Build one optional read-only ACP or GitHub evidence capture/shadow path outside Kernel, measuring mapping failures and native status discrepancies.
  • Independently test a second different source (FLOP/Butler or CEMS) with saved fixtures. Avoid generalizing source-specific results.
  • Complete at least one neutral recipient-side verification attempt; classify UNKNOWN or inconclusive honestly.
  • Continue B2 case collection, X1 preparatory work and AP2 blindness separately.
  • Measure engineering hours, time-to-test and external waiting separately. No new external fork without a reproduced upstream-native issue.

docs.title: Days 31–60: expand interoperability where the first witnesses justify it
docs.text:
• Compare a second protocol family: AP2, UCP, x402, A2A or MCP using their documented native capabilities and synthetic/no-spend negative vectors.
  • Improve reuse of observation/admission contract outside Kernel; do not coerce fractional or unrepresentable source data to pass restricted canonicalization.
  • If evidence shows a material canonical contract gap, write a scoped ADR and independent falsifier. Only then implement a Kernel change via protected CI and explicit owner approval.
  • Keep native PR review/release independent from local adapter viability.

docs.title: Days 61–90: decide from measured evidence
docs.text:
• Assess source-specific failures, integration reuse and recurring operational cost versus native alternatives.
  • Publish only claims supported by current Kernel and named independently reviewed recipient witnesses.
  • Pursue an authorized external pilot with bounded permissions and a clearly identified user or buyer when justified.
  • For each lane: GO (named next action), HOLD (specific missing dependency), STOP (falsified or prohibitive risk). Other lanes remain open.

docs.title: Permanent boundaries
docs.text:
P0 remains simulated PASS WITH BOUNDARY; B2-REAL 0/10 and 0/5 are not silently inflated; Level 0/X1 and AP2 Pass B have distinct frozen methods; T0 controlled harness is not external authority. No wallet funding/payment, deployment, new public claim, or external-system mutation without separate permission. No alternate canonical receipt or decision path in adapters.

Success is independently reproducible native benefit plus portable evidence that can be verified within its stated limits, not number of forks or PRs.

See Scoped Stop-Build Amendment, Open Collaboration, Contribution Protocol, Target map.

docs.text: Snapshot: 2026-10-12. Repositories were checked as public and not archived via connected GitHub metadata. Targeting is an internal research priority, NOT a partner agreement, product endorsement or proof of operational integration.

docs.title: Selection rule
docs.text:
Rate each candidate 0–5 on: real upstream user problem (35%), narrow testable patch (25%), proximity to PayGod trust boundary (20%), maintainer access/community clarity (10%), low risk or no-spend implementation (10%). Scores are candidate hypotheses and must be recomputed from issue/CI evidence, not presented as market facts. Tier A first, Tier B read/reproduce, Tier C only after a grounded need.

Fork budget: 1 active external code fork at a time for the first 30 days; maximum 2 concurrently only when both have a working witness and maintainer engagement. A directory of candidate links is not a reason to fork.

docs.title: Explicit out-of-scope early targets
docs.text: A new cryptocurrency token, a replacement settlement chain, an ACP/TCLK fork with rewritten wire format, a mandatory PayGod SDK in upstream, a generic cross-industry DSL, or commercial bank integration without an authentic external partner witness. Reconsider only with concrete demand and ADR.

docs.title: Native integration architecture
docs.text:
Upstream event/receipt/observation -> independent capture with provenance -> explicit admission policy (WITHHELD on unknown mandatory fact) -> existing PayGod canonical path only if it can represent input -> portable original evidence and labeled mapping -> independent verifier -> diagnostic comparison with native state.

In shadow mode PayGod must not affect external action. An external enforcer is a SEPARATE future optional product that would require actual nonbypassability proof and owner/rail authorization.

docs.title: Diversity / anti-lock-in
docs.text: Prefer protocol-neutral evidence and adapters; every integration target gets at least one deliberate comparator to avoid optimising solely for the first partner's implementation. Example comparators: ACP vs A2A job, TCLK coordination vs x402 settlement, Butler duty vs signed supply-chain artifact, AP2 native verifier vs independent observer.

docs.title: What establishes a reciprocal relationship?
docs.text:
1. Upstream confirms a native problem, gives feedback or merges a useful fix.
  2. Our patch improves their native workflows without imposing PayGod.
  3. Their maintainers or external users independently repeat and validate a witness.
  4. Only then discuss optional joint adapters/test vectors and business exploration. No collaborator or partnership is claimed from an opened PR or GitHub issue.
